A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same underlying three-stage speech-translation framework, despite substantial renaming and revision. Their text, equations, figures and tables are readable, including v2's appendix; v1 contains no appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original CoVoST-2 and MuST-C translation results, ASR measurements, architecture comparisons, curriculum ablations and inference timings.

after.justification: V2 reports original FLEURS and CoVoST-2 experiments, scaling and ablation results, case studies, and appendix BLEU/COMET results.

M1.justification: The three-stage curriculum and encoder-adapter-LLM design remain. However, the intermediate task changes from generating transcription plus translation to generating translation alone, and instructions now identify both source and target languages (Table 1 in both versions). These are limited procedural adaptations beyond renaming.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates English-to-German/Japanese/Chinese translation on CoVoST-2 and MuST-C. V2 removes MuST-C, adds FLEURS evaluations covering 6×12 and 15×14 directions, and reports multilingual Common Voice ASR training. CoVoST-2 coverage is retained, with additional evaluation of FLEURS-trained models.

E2.justification: The corresponding CoVoST-2 comparison drops SALMONN, BLSP-KD, GenTranslate variants and several Seamless configurations, while adding Qwen2.5-based cascades and direct instruction-tuning baselines. FLEURS comparisons additionally evaluate LoRA-adapted SeamlessM4T-V2. SALMONN and BLSP-KD remaining in related work does not preserve their experimental participation.

E3.justification: New FLEURS protocols introduce 52/129-hour S2TT training budgets, Qwen2.5 configurations at 3B/7B/32B, and LoRA controls. V2 adds COMET and Japanese char-versus-ja-mecab evaluation. The retained inference-speed table also changes its stated precision from bf16 to FP16; this does not establish that timings were rerun.

E4.justification: Curriculum ablations expand from en-zh to all three CoVoST-2 target languages. V2 adds MT-versus-S2TT comparisons, model/data scaling analyses and language-mixing error analysis, while replacing the original case studies and encoder/LLM combination analysis. The original MuST-C zero-shot investigation is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's additional averages, COMET scores and score-trend plot remain point-estimate reporting rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive FLEURS results, including 20.6/21.4/24.6 average BLEU for its 3B/7B/32B models in Table 3 and COMET results in Table 15. CoVoST-2 and ablation values are revised, and MuST-C results disappear. Changed models and settings prevent interpreting these replacements as same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The formal intermediate-task definition changes from producing both Y and Z in v1 Section 2 to producing only Z in v2 Section 2.1. Additional adapter equations and dimensional specifications mainly document implementation; neither version introduces theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from activating multimodal chain-of-thought and achieving selected CoVoST-2/MuST-C improvements to transferring LLM translation capabilities into low-resource, many-to-many S2TT. V2 adds claims of state-of-the-art average performance across 210 directions and the first supporting MLLM at 32B scale.

C2.justification: The inherited MT-capability explanation gains new interpretations involving English-data scarcity, MT/S2TT score correspondence and language mixing. V1's hardware limitation to models up to 8B is replaced by a substantive applicability boundary: performance and language coverage depend on the underlying LLM's translation capabilities.

D1.justification: V2 adds metric signatures and appendix settings covering Common Voice 19 training hours, stage-specific steps and learning rates, query dimensions, LoRA configurations and trainable parameter counts. It reports A100 training hardware and runtimes and changes the release information to a dedicated code-and-model repository. V1's CPU/RAM and software-version details are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 removes the standalone CoT discussion and associated foundational citations, repositioning the contribution around low-resource transfer learning with Pham et al. and Mueller et al. It also updates the multimodal-model discussion with Li et al. and Qwen2.5-Omni. This changes the research positioning substantially.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodological explanation and conclusion are extensively rewritten. CoT-ST/SLM/MMT terminology becomes LLM-SRT/MLLM/SMT, problem formulation is integrated into methodology, and experimental discussion is reorganized with a new appendix.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redrawn, and Figure 3 adds an MT/S2TT score comparison. Benchmark, multitask, ablation and case-study tables are restructured or replaced, with new appendix tables for languages, training settings and detailed results. The inference-time table is largely retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical grounding and reproducibility through matched instruction-tuning baselines, MT/S2TT comparisons across 210 directions, and detailed training, LoRA and metric specifications absent from v1. These improve support for the curriculum and its transfer-learning interpretation. MuST-C evidence is lost, and some claims overreach: the 32B 'all directions' statement conflicts with Table 3's English-source scores of 32.5 versus SeamlessM4T-V2's 33.1. Nevertheless, the stronger validation and transparency provide a substantial net improvement.
